title: Tempo-Adjusted Opportunity Scorer (TAOS): a time-aware RICE alternative for latency/cost sensitive roadmaps
creator: Evan Brooks
description: Problem: our current RICE-heavy scoring surfaces high-value opportunities but underweights time-decay of value, latency sensitivity, and engineering commit risk. Teams keep reprioritizing mid-cycle because opportunity windows close (partnerships, market timing) or because latency/cost tradeoffs change. Goal: design and pilot a lightweight, explainable scoring framework — TAOS — that is time-aware, explicitly models latency/cost sensitivity, and factors in implementation risk so PMs and Eng can make cycle-aware tradeoffs consistently.
decision_rationale: We need a practical alternative that keeps the intuitive parts of RICE (Reach, Impact) but adds two dimensions we repeatedly see cause rework: tempo (time-sensitivity of the opportunity) and commit risk (engineering complexity and rollback/maintenance cost). TAOS multiplies Opportunity Score by a tempo decay and divides by a risk-adjusted cost factor. This produces a ranked list that elevates near-term high-impact, low-latency-risk items while still surfacing long-term bets.
acceptance_criteria: Prototype scoring spreadsheet and script that outputs ranked backlog for a sample of 50 roadmap items
At least two cross-functional PM/Eng/Design reviews with documented feedback and one iteration on formula
Pilot applied to Q2 roadmap: 20 items rescored; at least 3 items reclassified to higher priority vs current RICE baseline and accepted by triage
Scoring explainability doc and one-pager created and linked in Confluence
